plan.goal: Find and rank representative sequences for NAD(P)HX repair proteins annotated with ADP-dependent NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase activity (GO:0034591) and NADPHX epimerase activity (GO:0034589), using sequence-level biochemical analysis and parallel literature context.
assumptions: GO:0034591 corresponds to ADP-dependent NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase (NADHX dehydratase) molecular function; GO:0034589 corresponds to NADPHX epimerase molecular function — both are established GO identifiers for the NAD(P)HX repair pathway.
No taxonomic restriction is applied; cross-organism retrieval maximizes representation of the bifunctional bacterial enzyme (YjeF-like) and monofunctional eukaryotic homologs.
Both Swiss-Prot and TrEMBL entries are included (reviewed filter omitted) for broad sequence-space coverage.
Deduplication removes identical sequences appearing under multiple accessions or organisms.
Sequence analysis at pH 7.4 captures net charge, compositional features, and domain-like regions relevant to NAD-binding Rossmann-fold topology and cofactor-binding pockets.

Dehydratase-annotated sequences serve as the primary candidate set for rank_designs because they are more taxonomically widespread and include bifunctional enzyme representatives; the epimerase analysis is passed as a supplementary analysis layer to enable cross-activity scoring.
Literature evidence is collected in parallel and informs ranking rationale without blocking the retrieval or analysis steps.
No structural prediction or generative tools are required for a sequence-understanding and ranking task.
